solutionSource.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

entries.clue: All the best working dogs went (8)

indicatorNotes.working: the dogs are put to work, knocked into a new order

blocks.note: went = urinated, as a dog does

annotation.surface: A report that the finest sheepdogs have all left the trial.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Went' looks like plain departure; here it is the dog's other business. 'All the best' is the farewell wish.
annotation.definitionFit: Godspeed is a wish of good luck to someone setting out, as is 'all the best'.

entries.clue: Respect part in audition experiencing continuing success (2,1,4)

indicatorNotes.in audition: audition is hearing, so what follows is judged by sound

blocks.note: honour said with a silent H

annotation.surface: An actor is getting a good response to a part at audition and keeps landing roles.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Audition' sounds like the theatre and fits 'part', but it is here in its root sense of hearing.
annotation.definitionFit: To be on a roll is to be enjoying a run of successes.

entries.clue: Rows with pet shop about spectacular event (11)

indicatorNotes.about: the letters are turned about, moved round

annotation.surface: Arguments break out at a pet shop over some big happening.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rows' is read as quarrels in the surface, but only its letters matter.
annotation.definitionFit: A showstopper is a performance or event so striking it halts the show with applause.

entries.clue: Heading north, cavalrymen easily suppressing hostile forces (5)

indicatorNotes.Heading north: in a down clue, going north means reading upwards
indicatorNotes.suppressing: the two words hold the answer pressed down inside them

blocks.note: the letters run across the gap between the two words, from the end of cavalrymen into the first letter of easily, and are read upwards

annotation.surface: Horsemen riding north easily hold down the opposing army.
annotation.walkthrough: The cavalry and hostile forces make one battlefield, so the hidden letters slip by.
annotation.definitionFit: The enemy is the hostile force one fights, collectively singular.

entries.clue: Make bet for wealthy old lady (7)

blocks.note: make = do, as in do a cake

annotation.surface: Someone places a bet on behalf of a rich elderly woman.
annotation.walkthrough: A dowager strictly is a widow holding a title or property from her late husband, hence wealthy.
annotation.definitionFit: A dowager is a dignified elderly woman of means, typically a widow with inherited rank.

entries.clue: Blunder, almost hugging new primate (6)

indicatorNotes.almost: the word stops one letter short
indicatorNotes.hugging: the shortened word wraps round the new letter

blocks.note: BOOBOO, a blunder, less its last letter

annotation.surface: A zookeeper's mistake: nearly cuddling the latest ape.
annotation.walkthrough: A booboo is informal for a blunder. The surface reads as a zookeeper's gaffe, with the primate already in the picture.
annotation.definitionFit: The bonobo is a great ape, close cousin of the chimpanzee, and so a primate.

entries.clue: Part of seat higher for broadcast, which is a bloomer (9)

indicatorNotes.for broadcast: what is broadcast is heard, so the words count by sound

blocks.note: a buttock is part of the seat, the backside; higher = up

annotation.surface: A seat part raised for a TV programme turns out to be a gaffe.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' suggests a blunder, as the surface wants; it is here something that blooms. Said quickly, 'buttock up' becomes 'buttercup'.
annotation.definitionFit: A buttercup is a flower, and a flower is something that blooms.

entries.clue: Engage regularly? In Perth, no (3)

indicatorNotes.regularly: something done regularly happens at even intervals, so the letters are taken at even steps, every second one

blocks.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of engage

annotation.surface: Asking whether to get involved every so often, and getting a Scottish refusal.
annotation.walkthrough: Perth here is the Scottish city, not the Australian one, which makes 'no' Scots dialect NAE.
annotation.definitionFit: A regional use: in Scots dialect, as spoken in Perth, this is how no is said.

entries.clue: Nomad’s become settled around Oxford University (7)

indicatorNotes.around: BED IN goes around the university

blocks.note: to bed in is to settle into place

annotation.surface: A wanderer has finally settled down near Oxford.
annotation.walkthrough: The 's is 'is', a link, not a possessive. The irony is the surface: the nomad has settled.
annotation.definitionFit: The Bedouin are desert Arabs traditionally living as nomads.

entries.clue: Perplexed, makes up for deficiencies with shortened broadcast (2,4,4,3)

blocks.note: to atone is to make amends

annotation.surface: Someone baffled, making good their shortcomings with a cut transmission.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Shortened' seems to belong to 'broadcast', but it trims the word before it.
annotation.definitionFit: At one's wits' end means so baffled one does not know what to do.

entries.clue: Rebellious, throw to the left, then throw to the right (6)

indicatorNotes.to the left: in an across clue, going left means reading backwards

blocks.note: LOB, a throw, written right to left
a shy is a throw, read normally

annotation.surface: A rebel hurls things left and right in a tantrum.
annotation.walkthrough: 'To the right' just confirms normal reading; the left and right also nod at political wings. A shy is a throw, as in coconut shy.
annotation.definitionFit: Bolshy, from Bolshevik, is British slang for uncooperative or rebellious.

entries.clue: Dull lecture announced extinct bird (5,3)

indicatorNotes.announced: spoken out loud, so judged by sound

annotation.surface: A boring talk is given about a vanished species.
annotation.walkthrough: The split moves: GREY TALK is heard as GREAT AUK.
annotation.definitionFit: The great auk was a large flightless seabird hunted to extinction in 1844.

entries.clue: Bouncer’s two modes of transport across river (11)

indicatorNotes.across: the river sits between the two transports, as a crossing

annotation.surface: A nightclub doorman commutes by two vehicles across a river.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bouncer' suggests a doorman; it is someone who bounces on a trampoline.
annotation.definitionFit: A trampoliner bounces for sport, so is literally a bouncer.

entries.clue: Work at probing every Republican in charge of different geographical areas (10)

indicatorNotes.probing: a probe goes into something, so OP AT goes inside

annotation.surface: A political researcher studies every Republican who runs a different region.
annotation.walkthrough: Work is OP from opus, a musical work. The insertion lands after the first three letters of the surrounding string.
annotation.definitionFit: Allopatric, in biology, describes species or populations occurring in separate geographical areas.

entries.clue: Attacker of creature, one with six feet, having internal trouble (9)

indicatorNotes.having internal: the pair has the trouble inside it

annotation.surface: An attacker of some animal, an insect with a stomach upset.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Six feet' tempts toward height or a grave; it is legs.
annotation.definitionFit: An assailant is someone who attacks another.

entries.clue: Problem of teenagers in north contained by expert (4)

indicatorNotes.contained by: to be contained by something is to be held within it, so the expert holds the N inside

annotation.surface: Teenage troubles in northern England being handled by a specialist.
annotation.walkthrough: An ace, from the ace fighter pilot, is the crossword's usual expert.
annotation.definitionFit: Acne, spots on the skin, is the classic teenage complaint.

entries.clue: Lacking in energy, male stops backchat (4)

indicatorNotes.stops: M stops up LIP, plugging it from inside

annotation.surface: A tired man stops answering back.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Stops' reads as halts; it is the stopper in a bottle. 'Backchat' is British for cheeky answering back.
annotation.definitionFit: Limp means floppy, lacking firmness or vigour.

entries.clue: Vice-admiral blocking popular article from German aggressor (7)

indicatorNotes.blocking: VA stands in the way between IN and DER

annotation.surface: A naval officer stands in the way of a popular piece about a German attacker.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Article' reads as a newspaper piece; it is the grammatical article DER.
annotation.definitionFit: An invader is one who attacks and enters another's territory, an aggressor.

entries.clue: Cops kept up with malfunctioning toy (4,6)

indicatorNotes.malfunctioning: the letters are not working as they should, so rearrange them

annotation.surface: Police stayed awake all night fixing a broken toy.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Kept up' looks like a reversal instruction, but it is only fodder.
annotation.definitionFit: A sock puppet is a simple toy made by pulling a sock over the hand.

entries.clue: John thanks nurses when playing card game (7)

indicatorNotes.nurses: to nurse is to hold close, so TA holds AS

annotation.surface: A man called John thanks the nurses during a game of cards.
annotation.walkthrough: John looks like a name; it is American slang for the toilet, as is CAN. TA is everyday British for thanks.
annotation.definitionFit: Canasta is a rummy-type game played with two packs of cards.

entries.clue: Important and valuable source found in English books (7)

indicatorNotes.found in: MINE is found inside the other letters

blocks.note: a mine of information, or of gold

annotation.surface: A key primary source turns up among English texts.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Books' is the standard NT (or OT) for the Testament.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: people of high standing who stand out from the crowd are important figures.

entries.clue: State is backed and supported by hatred (8)

indicatorNotes.backed: a car that is backed goes in reverse, so IS is written in reverse

blocks.note: to aver is to state firmly

annotation.surface: A political state finds itself backed and held up by animosity.
annotation.walkthrough: 'State' is the verb, not a nation.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, slightly softened: a deep-seated dislike, which at its strongest is hatred.

entries.clue: Fat reduced by half in round rice cake (6)

indicatorNotes.reduced by half: LARD keeps only its first half
indicatorNotes.in: the halved fat is put in the rice, placed inside it
indicatorNotes.round: to turn something round is to face it the other way, so RICE is read back to front

blocks.note: LARD, a fat, cut to two of its four letters

annotation.surface: A diet recipe halves the fat in a rice cake.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Rice cake' is one thing in the surface; the cake is the definition alone. LA goes into ECIR.
annotation.definitionFit: An eclair is a long choux pastry cake filled with cream.

entries.clue: Essentially, sent kid back for early computer (5)

indicatorNotes.Essentially: the essence of each word is its middle

annotation.surface: Someone returned a child's gadget for an old computer.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Back' looks like a reversal instruction, but it is the third word whose middle is taken.
annotation.definitionFit: ENIAC, built in 1945, was one of the first general-purpose electronic computers.

entries.clue: Horrific Icelandic mess in economics? (6,7)

annotation.surface: Iceland's economy after its 2008 banking crash was an awful mess.
annotation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the definition is a nickname: Thomas Carlyle called economics the dismal science in 1849.
annotation.definitionFit: The dismal science is a traditional mocking name for economics.

entries.clue: Witness search for missing king (3)

indicatorNotes.missing: a word missing something lacks it, so SEEK is left without its king

blocks.note: to search for is to seek

annotation.surface: Hunting for a witness to a king's disappearance.
annotation.walkthrough: SEEK loses its K.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym, both verbs: to witness an event is to watch it happen with your own eyes.

entries.clue: Meddles close to first minister (6)

indicatorNotes.close to: the close of a word is its last letter

annotation.surface: Someone interferes, staying close to the First Minister.
annotation.walkthrough: 'First Minister' reads as one title (Scotland and Wales have one); 'first' is only fodder for its last letter.
annotation.definitionFit: Definition by example: a minister of religion is any clergyman, and this is one kind.

entries.clue: Current price of copper is precise (8)

annotation.surface: A market report quoting today's copper price exactly.
annotation.walkthrough: Blocks run in answer order: the copper comes before the price.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a precise measurement is one correct to the last detail.
